domain_label: AI-Designed D2C Knitwear — Design Judgement & 3-Article Line Architecture
purpose: A method for reasoning about how the California D2C knitwear capsule is actually designed — the four upstream constraints that pre-decide the design space before any aesthetic choice, the silhouette-to-stitch-to-colour-to-detail shared spine, the texture-over-colour rule, the A1/A2/A3 fibre-role ladder with the loud-front/evergreen-behind architecture, the finished-garment grade and gauge/shrinkage interaction, and the Flux ideation-to-producible-spec bridge — tying every design choice to its upstream constraint and never confusing a cheap pretty render with a buildable tech pack.
assumptions: the design space is generated from upstream constraints (colour budget, warm-CA weight, linker throughput, anti-pill gate), not from a moodboard; the 2026 youth trend happens to reward the same choices, a coincidence to bank not to rely on, tagged estimate

all cost, price, MOQ, CAC, throughput and pilling-grade bands are estimate-not-fact: a method-plus-basis reasoned range with the literal word estimate and a confidence, never a researched per-unit quote; the only hard duty/legal anchors are public facts
US sweater duties are public facts: cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% (never cotton ~7%); fibre choice changes duty and feeds the price ladder

AI (Flux) is a near-zero-marginal-cost idea-and-content multiplier upstream of the programmer, never a knit compiler; a Flux pixel cannot specify the four buildability inputs and actively renders impossible knits, so a human programmer plus a physical PPS swatch always close the loop
sizing is finished-garment not body, on a unisex men's-derived block; the linear grade and the local size curve are launch hypotheses the Turlock pop-ups validate or break, not settled facts
exclusions: yarn sourcing, count selection and dye-lot procurement economics (owned by the yarn specialist; consumed here only as the colour-budget and fibre-hand constraints)

the CAD/flat-knit programmer's needle-action authoring, FF shaping and stitch-count program (owned by the machines specialist; this KB hands off the inch-grade and design intent, it does not write the program)
landed-cost, duty and unit-economics modelling and the price-floor computation (owned by the logistics specialist; price positions here are design-tier signals, not the margin model)
the brand/market acquisition funnel, CAC and channel economics (owned by the brand specialist; consumed here as the youth-front-door and warm-California-consumer constraints)
stating any specific live Flux parameter, model-version behaviour, or Central-Valley-youth micro-trend as a settled fact; those are snapshot or unknown and refused, not fabricated

competency_questions.question: What four upstream constraints decide the design space before any aesthetic choice, and what does each forbid or force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOUR_BUDGET_CEILING, WARM_CA_WEIGHT, LINKER_THROUGHPUT and ANTIPILL_GATE each state what the constraint forbids/forces and the design consequence it pre-decides, sourced to the yarn/machines/brand inputs

competency_questions.question: Why is the line colour-starved-not-style-starved, and what is the texture-over-colour rule that falls out of the colour budget?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEXTURE_OVER_COLOUR states the texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print, single-colour-body-with-at-most-a-contrast-tip rule as the consequence of the 2-4-colour dye-lot ceiling, and ties it to the 2026 trend alignment as a banked coincidence

competency_questions.question: What is the shared silhouette-to-stitch-to-colour-to-detail spine that all three articles inherit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SILHOUETTE_STITCH_SPINE names the soft-boxy relaxed-straight unisex block with two variants off one block, STITCH_PALETTE_MAP maps the use/sparing/avoid stitch tiers to gauge/colour/machine, and COLOUR_ARCHITECTURE gives the 2-anchor-plus-1-2-accent rule

competency_questions.question: What is the A1 cotton-blend core's role, and why is it the evergreen margin and LTV engine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A1_COTTON_CORE states the 12GG cotton-blend evergreen role, the longest sell-window, the do-not-over-elaborate rule, and the ~16.5% cotton duty anchor feeding its price tier

competency_questions.question: Why is A2 fine-acrylic the loud-but-cheap youth front door, and why must it stay anti-pill-conservative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A2_ACRYLIC_FRONTDOOR states the 7-12GG acrylic acquisition role, the loud trend-accent colour, the smooth-tight no-float conservative stitch, the brand-ending pilling-video stake, and the ~32% MMF duty anchor

competency_questions.question: What is A3 merino/lambswool's halo/price-anchor role, and why does cable plus fashioning marks have to be priced in?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A3_MERINO_HALO states the thin merino/lambswool Nov-Feb premium role, cable plus fine links-links plus fashioning marks as FF-authenticity, the extra yarn and linker cost it must price for, and the ~16% wool duty anchor

competency_questions.question: Why exactly three articles and not two or four, and how do they form a fibre-role ladder rather than a style count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WHY_EXACTLY_THREE shows each article occupies a distinct economic role the others cannot fill (margin engine / front door / halo), that three is the MOQ-survivable maximum (~54 SKUs) and the role-complete minimum, and that a fourth breaks the dye-lot ceiling while a second forfeits a role

competency_questions.question: What is the loud-front/evergreen-behind architecture rule and why does it bind?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOUD_FRONT_EVERGREEN states that the loud youth A2 sits at the acquisition front while the durable A1 margin engine sits behind, and that if the A2 youth capsule visually becomes the house brand, margin and longevity erode

competency_questions.question: How is the line sized on a finished-garment grade, and why is finished-not-body the number-one error to avoid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISHED_GARMENT_GRADE states the XS-XXL unisex finished-garment specs with ~5-6 inch ease, the four knit measurements with the M base, and the linear grade (chest +2 in/size, body +1.5, sleeve +0.75, hem +2, full-chest 38-48)

competency_questions.question: How do gauge, grade and shrinkage interact so the inch-grade becomes a knittable spec, and why is this the knit-unique step?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GAUGE_GRADE_SHRINK states the whole-wales/courses translation at production density, the build-to-post-wash-target rule on a washed swatch, the per-fibre knit-larger allowance, and tolerance-every-point or the grade is decorative

competency_questions.question: How do the Turlock pop-ups function as the fitting lab that sets the production size curve?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POPUP_FITTING_LAB states the pop-ups capture the local size curve and validate grade/ease on the ~46%-Hispanic Central-Valley body, buy down the ~24% online return rate, and run as an iteration loop not a one-time calibration

competency_questions.question: How is trend ingested through a three-filter funnel and turned into a four-drop release calendar without chasing the runway?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TREND_DROP_CALENDAR states the macro/meso/micro filter funnel where only signals surviving all three and the four constraints enter the line, the owned-but-refused Central-Valley-youth hype gap, and the D1-D4 calendar ordered ahead of the Jul-Oct Ludhiana peak

competency_questions.question: What is Flux in this pipeline, what can a render specify, and what are the four buildability inputs it cannot?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLUX_IDEATION_ROLE states Flux is an idea-and-content engine upstream of the programmer not a knit compiler, and BUILDABILITY_BRIDGE names the four inputs a pixel cannot give (yarn count, true GG/density, stitch-count grade, finished measurements/shrinkage) mapped to who fills each

competency_questions.question: Given the constraints, the buildability gap and the impossible-knit/pilling/colourwork traps, what is the merged go/no-go on shipping a designed look to Ludhiana?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRODUCIBILITY_GATE composes the four constraints, the buildability bridge and the three traps into a defensible ship/hold verdict that kills impossible knits, un-payable colourwork and pill-prone acrylic before a PPS swatch and tech pack are locked

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every money/MOQ/CAC/throughput/pilling-grade band in this KB: a reasoned range carrying method, basis and confidence and the literal word estimate, never a researched per-unit quote; only public duty rates and cited trend/colour facts are tagged fact.

The design spine that falls out of the 2-4-colour dye-lot ceiling: interest is carried by stitch architecture (rib, half-Milano, cable, pointelle) and silhouette, with a single-colour body and at most a contrast rib or tip, because the budget cannot pay for multi-colour pattern.

The reason there are exactly three articles: A1 cotton-blend is the margin/LTV engine, A2 fine-acrylic is the cheap youth front door bought for reach not contribution, A3 merino/lambswool is the halo/price-anchor; each occupies a distinct economic role the others cannot fill, so dropping one loses a function.
The binding architecture rule: design A2 loud at the acquisition front and A1 evergreen behind it; if the loud youth capsule visually becomes the house brand, margin and longevity erode.

The tech-pack measurement convention used throughout: flat/half garment measurements (body chest plus ~5-6 inch sweater layering ease equals garment chest), graded as the garment then sanity-checked against body charts; confusing finished with body ships a sweater a full size off.

The brand-ending acceptance gate on acrylic A2: no long floats or brushed-fuzzy surfaces, a smooth tight conservative stitch plus a contractual anti-pill spec and an ICI/Martindale pilling grade target post-wash, because one pilling video is brand-ending and acrylic pills worst.

The four things that make a knit buildable and that a Flux pixel cannot specify: yarn count plus fibre plus blend ratio, true gauge (GG) plus stitch density, panel shaping plus stitch-count grade, and finished measurements plus tolerances plus shrinkage allowance; each is filled from the yarn spec, the sizing math, the CAD programmer and the PPS swatch.

A render flaw Flux actively produces: non-stitch-conserving cables, ribs that change wale count, or seamless joins no linker makes; the top offenders are A3's cable and fashioning marks, caught in human spec review before any dye-lot money moves, not by the prompt.

The physical pre-production-sample swatch that measures real gauge, stitch density and shrinkage and confirms the post-wash pilling grade; the swatch, not the render or the screen colour, is the truth that closes the design-to-make loop.

The release clock reconciling the warm-California sell-window (light/transitional ~Sept-April, true heavy wool only Nov-Feb), the Ludhiana production clock (yarn-in to ex-factory ~6-12 weeks, ordered ahead of the Jul-Oct cluster peak), and the trend clock (accents picked 1-2 quarters ahead); D1 Fall core, D2 Holiday premium, D3 Youth accent, D4 Spring transitional.

nodes.definition: Establish the first and most design-defining upstream constraint: the dye-lot MOQ (~150-500 kg per colour, estimate from yarn) caps a launch at roughly 2-4 colours, which the working capital cannot exceed. This forbids multi-colour Fair-Isle, jacquard and 6-colour print, and forces the line to be colour-starved-not-style-starved: interest must come from stitch and silhouette, not colour-count. Every aesthetic choice downstream lives inside this ceiling; it is the single biggest pre-aesthetic fact, set before a moodboard is opened.

included: the 2-4-colour launch ceiling from the dye-lot MOQ
what colourwork it forbids
the colour-starved-not-style-starved consequence
excluded: the yarn procurement and dye-lot economics themselves (yarn specialist)
the specific stitch palette (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the colour ceiling as constraint number one stops the line from being designed around colour the budget cannot fund
pros.example: a 6-colour jacquard concept is declined at the brief stage because it needs four dye lots the launch cannot pay for

cons.claim: A hard colour ceiling can be read as forbidding any hero colour rather than as a discipline to prove one before paying for it
cons.example: refusing a single accent that sell-through would justify because the ceiling is applied too rigidly

failure_modes: designing a multi-colour pattern the dye-lot budget cannot fund and discovering it at the PO
treating colour-count as the interest lever when the ceiling forces it onto stitch
acceptance_tests: the constraint states the ~2-4-colour launch ceiling from the dye-lot MOQ as an estimate, what colourwork it forbids, and the colour-starved-not-style-starved consequence it pre-decides
revisit_triggers: the dye-lot MOQ or per-colour kg band is re-quoted in the yarn spec
sell-through proves a hero colour worth a second dye lot
shared-dye-lot economics across articles change the colour math

base.update_signal: the dye-lot MOQ, per-colour cost, or shared-lot economics change

nodes.definition: Establish the second upstream constraint: the warm-California market sells heavy wool only ~Nov-Feb, so the line is fine-gauge 12GG at ~200-350 g (estimate from yarn GG-to-weight map), an elevated-basic canvas, not a chunky 3-5GG hero knit. This forbids alpine-heritage bulk and forces the line to fake substance with surface stitch (cable, half-Milano) rather than bulky yarn. It also pushes slightly-oversized layering-friendly fits, because in a warm climate a sweater is worn open, not as sole insulation.

included: the 12GG ~200-350 g warm-CA weight band
the no-chunky/no-alpine forbiddance
the fake-substance-with-surface-stitch consequence
excluded: the GG-to-yarn-count match (yarn specialist)
the specific colour palette

pros.claim: Fixing the weight at fine-gauge ties the whole aesthetic to the climate the brand actually sells into
pros.example: a chunky funnel-neck concept is rejected because it reads alpine and sells only two months in warm California

cons.claim: A fine-gauge-only rule can under-serve the genuine Nov-Feb true-cold window that does carry a heavier premium piece
cons.example: treating all wool as out when A3 is precisely the thin Nov-Feb premium the window allows

failure_modes: designing chunky 3-5GG hero knits that sell only two warm-California months
leaning on bulky yarn for substance when surface stitch is the warm-climate trick
acceptance_tests: the constraint states the 12GG ~200-350 g warm-CA weight band as an estimate, what bulk it forbids, and the fake-substance-with-surface-stitch consequence
revisit_triggers: the GG-to-weight band is re-quoted in the yarn spec
the California sell-window read shifts
a true-cold premium piece needs a heavier gauge than 12GG

base.update_signal: the warm-CA weight band or sell-window read changes

nodes.definition: Establish the third upstream constraint: linking (loop-to-loop seaming) is the throughput bottleneck and a real capacity cost, so every extra fully-fashioned panel, colour-block join or seam is linker minutes spent. This forces the design toward fewer, cleaner seams and reserves fashioning marks and cable as a priced A3 authenticity cue rather than an everywhere default. The constraint is why two silhouette variants come off one block, not three base shapes, and why cable plus fashioning marks must be priced for the extra linker time they add.

included: linking as throughput bottleneck and capacity cost
the fewer-cleaner-seams design push
fashioning marks/cable as priced A3 cues
excluded: the machine programming and linker operation (machines specialist)
the per-minute linker cost model (logistics specialist)

pros.claim: Treating linker minutes as a design cost keeps seam count and fashioning honest rather than decorative
pros.example: reserving visible fashioning marks for A3 instead of every article, because each mark is priced linker time

cons.claim: Over-minimising seams can strip the FF-authenticity cues that justify the A3 premium
cons.example: removing fashioning marks entirely and losing the visible proof that A3 is genuinely fully-fashioned

failure_modes: proliferating panels and colour-block joins that consume scarce linker capacity
spreading cable and fashioning marks across all articles instead of pricing them into A3
acceptance_tests: the constraint states linking as the throughput bottleneck, the fewer-cleaner-seams push, and that cable/fashioning marks must be priced as A3 cues for the linker time they add
revisit_triggers: the linker capacity or per-seam cost is re-quoted by machines/logistics
a whole-garment option removes the linking step
a fashioning-heavy design is proposed beyond A3

base.update_signal: linker capacity, per-seam cost, or a whole-garment option changes

nodes.definition: Establish the fourth upstream constraint, a brand-ending acceptance gate specific to acrylic A2: no long floats or brushed-fuzzy surfaces, because acrylic pills fastest and one pilling video is brand-ending (brand input). This forces A2 to run a smooth, tight, conservative stitch plus a contractual anti-pill spec and an ICI/Martindale pilling-grade target (estimate ~3-4 post-wash) written into the PO. The gate overrules aesthetics: if a prettier fuzzy render appears for A2, it is rejected no matter how good it looks, because the real defence is the anti-pill grade and tight gauge, not the image.

included: the no-float/no-brush acrylic gate
the smooth-tight-conservative-stitch plus contractual anti-pill spec
the pilling-grade target as the real defence
excluded: the anti-pill finish chemistry and yarn twist (yarn/finishing specialists)
the pilling lab test method detail (quality specialist)

pros.claim: Making anti-pill a binding gate, not a preference, protects the front-door article from the one defect that ends the brand
pros.example: rejecting a gorgeous brushed-fuzzy A2 render because the surface that photographs best pills worst

cons.claim: A hard anti-pill gate narrows A2's surface vocabulary to tight smooth stitches, limiting its visual range
cons.example: declining a soft hand-feel finish that would lift A2's appeal but fail the pilling grade

failure_modes: shipping a brushed or floated acrylic surface that pills and triggers a brand-ending return wave
trusting a smooth render instead of the contractual anti-pill grade and tight gauge
acceptance_tests: the gate states the no-float/no-brush rule on acrylic, the smooth-tight conservative stitch plus contractual anti-pill spec and pilling-grade target as estimate, and that it overrules a prettier fuzzy render
revisit_triggers: the acrylic blend or anti-pill finish spec changes in the yarn input
a pilling-grade test result lands below target on a PPS swatch
the brand reports a pilling-driven return signal

base.update_signal: the acrylic anti-pill spec, twist, or a pilling-grade result changes

nodes.definition: State the design rule that falls directly out of the colour-budget ceiling: texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print, single-colour body with at most a contrast rib or tip. Interest is carried by stitch architecture (rib, half-Milano, cable, pointelle) and silhouette, never by colour the budget cannot pay for. This is also the 2026 youth direction (boxy/oversized plus rib/cable revival plus pigment-return), so constraint and fashion align, a coincidence worth banking but not relying on. It is the spine every article inherits and the first filter on any trend signal.

included: the texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print rule
single-colour body with at most a contrast tip
the banked 2026-trend alignment
excluded: the specific stitch tiers (stitch-palette node)
the colour anchors/accents (colour-architecture node)

pros.claim: Converting the colour ceiling into a positive texture-over-colour rule gives the whole line one coherent aesthetic engine
pros.example: a full-body 2x2 rib hero reads as designed interest while costing only one dye lot

cons.claim: Banking the trend alignment can tempt over-reliance on a fashion direction that may turn before the constraint does
cons.example: treating the rib/cable revival as permanent and being caught when the silhouette moves while the budget stays fixed

failure_modes: reaching for colour to create interest when the budget forces it onto stitch
relying on the trend alignment instead of the constraint that actually pre-decides the rule
acceptance_tests: the rule states texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print, single-colour-body-with-at-most-a-contrast-tip, derived from the colour ceiling and flagged as trend-aligned coincidence
revisit_triggers: the colour ceiling changes
the 2026 boxy/rib/cable trend direction shifts
a texture-heavy design proves to under-photograph for the consumer

base.update_signal: the colour ceiling or the boxy/rib/cable trend direction changes

nodes.definition: Define the shared core fit block all three articles inherit: a relaxed-straight / soft-boxy cut with dropped or soft-set shoulder, straight-to-slightly-tapered body and ~5-6 inch ease (top of the standard 4-6 inch sweater layering band, fact), graded XS-XXL and gender-neutral. SKU discipline takes two silhouette variants off the one block, a crew/mock pullover (the volume seller, simplest to link) and a cardigan or quarter-zip (layering), with no third base shape at launch. Crop is reserved for the A2 youth drop; heavy shawl-collar and chunky funnel necks are banned as alpine.

included: the relaxed-straight soft-boxy block with ~5-6 inch ease
two variants off one block, no third base shape
the gender-neutral unisex cut and the alpine-neck ban
excluded: the finished-garment grade math (sizing node)
the per-article stitch choices (stitch-palette and article nodes)

pros.claim: One block with two variants holds SKU count down while still covering the volume and layering needs
pros.example: a crew pullover and a cardigan sharing the same graded block instead of three independently engineered shapes

cons.claim: A single block can feel repetitive across articles if stitch and colour do not carry the differentiation
cons.example: three articles reading as one sweater because only the block, not the surface, varies

failure_modes: adding a third base shape at launch and multiplying SKU and linker cost
drifting into alpine shawl/funnel necks the warm-California brand bans
acceptance_tests: the spine states the soft-boxy ~5-6 inch-ease unisex block, the two-variants-off-one-block rule with no third base shape, and the alpine-neck ban
revisit_triggers: the layering-ease band or unisex-block convention is revised
a pop-up signal argues for a different base shape
the warm-climate worn-open assumption changes

base.update_signal: the fit block, ease band, or variant count changes

nodes.definition: Map the stitch palette to the constraints in three tiers. USE freely (single-colour, texture as interest): jersey, rib 1x1/2x2 as cuffs/hems and as a full-body hero, half-Milano/Milano/half-cardigan to fake density at fine gauge, cable as texture-value (more yarn plus machine time, so priced premium/A3), and links-links/purl plus pointelle for lightweight warm-CA spring. USE sparingly (colour-cheap): plating for a luxe face at near-zero colour cost, and tipping/contrast rib from the 2-4-colour budget. AVOID or reserve (colour-hungry or pill-risky): jacquard (multi-colour back-floats that pill on acrylic) and intarsia (slow, viable only as a single hero graphic on one premium drop).

included: the use-freely / use-sparingly / avoid-or-reserve stitch tiers
each tier mapped to the colour, gauge, machine and pill constraints
cable and intarsia as priced or reserved exceptions
excluded: the machine capability to knit a structure (machines specialist)
the per-article assignment (article nodes)

pros.claim: Tiering stitches by which constraint gates them turns the palette into a constraint-respecting toolkit
pros.example: half-Milano chosen to fake substance at fine gauge instead of a chunky yarn the climate rejects

cons.claim: A tiered palette can read as forbidding colourwork outright when one reserved intarsia hero is still allowed
cons.example: ruling out a single premium-drop intarsia graphic that the tiering actually permits

failure_modes: using jacquard or floated colourwork that the budget cannot fund and that pills on acrylic
treating cable as free when it adds yarn and linker cost that must be priced into A3
acceptance_tests: the map states the three stitch tiers, each tied to the colour/gauge/machine/pill constraint that gates it, with cable priced and intarsia reserved to one premium hero
revisit_triggers: a machine-capability change enables or disables a structure
the colour budget or anti-pill spec changes a tier
a reserved intarsia hero is proposed for a drop

base.update_signal: a machine capability, colour budget, or anti-pill spec changes a stitch tier

nodes.definition: Define the colour system inside the 2-4-colour ceiling: two evergreen anchors plus one to two rotating accents. Anchors are a warm off-white/cream plus a mid neutral (oat/greige/soft charcoal) that read clean-Californian, with 2026 Pantone Cloud Dancer making the anchor on-trend (fact). Accents (<=2 at a time, rotated per drop) are AW26 runway knit colours such as eggplant/plum, marigold/butter, teal and pillar-box red (fact), or the softer Gen-Z icy-blue/pastel read (estimate). Hero-colour discipline: prove a hero on sell-through before paying a small-batch surcharge or a second dye lot; launch ~2 anchors plus 1 accent. Colour names and any slogan-knit must clear a Spanish reading (mandatory, ~46% Hispanic).

included: the 2-anchor-plus-1-2-accent rule
the cream/neutral anchors and the rotating trend accents
hero-colour discipline and the Spanish-reading clearance
excluded: the dye-lot procurement (yarn specialist)
screen-colour-to-dye-shade gap (buildability node)

pros.claim: Splitting colour into stable anchors and rotating accents lets the line feel fresh while sharing dye lots
pros.example: two evergreen anchors carried across all three articles with one rotating accent on the A2 youth drop

cons.claim: A fixed anchor pair can read as safe or repetitive if the rotating accent is too timid to signal newness
cons.example: an accent so close to the neutral that a drop reads identical to the last

failure_modes: funding a hero colour before sell-through proves it
shipping a colour name or slogan-knit that fails a Spanish reading in a ~46%-Hispanic market
acceptance_tests: the architecture states the 2-anchor-plus-1-2-accent rule with the cream/neutral anchors and rotating accents, the hero-before-second-dye-lot discipline, and the Spanish-reading clearance
revisit_triggers: the Pantone or AW26 runway palette is updated
sell-through proves or kills a hero colour
a slogan-knit or colour name needs Spanish clearance

base.update_signal: the trend palette, a hero sell-through result, or a Spanish-clearance need changes

nodes.definition: Model A1, the cotton-blend 12GG core: the margin and LTV engine with the longest sell-window (~Sept-April) and the best repeat. Silhouette is the relaxed-straight unisex crew plus one cardigan at true length; stitch is jersey plus full rib plus half-Milano for substance with clean self-finish; colour is the two anchors (cream plus neutral). Price tier ~$70-95 (positioning estimate; logistics sets floors), feeding off the cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% duty (fact). The binding design rule is do-not-over-elaborate the margin engine: A1 stays evergreen and clean so it outlives any drop, the article the brand is built to repeat-sell.

included: A1's margin/LTV evergreen role and longest sell-window
its silhouette/stitch/colour and ~$70-95 tier estimate
the cotton ~16.5% duty anchor and do-not-over-elaborate rule
excluded: the cotton yarn count/blend procurement (yarn specialist)
the price-floor margin model (logistics specialist)

pros.claim: Keeping A1 evergreen and clean makes it the durable repeat-sell engine the brand's LTV rests on
pros.example: a plain ribbed cotton crew that sells across seasons and drives repeat purchase rather than chasing a trend

cons.claim: An evergreen core risks being seen as boring if it is not refreshed via anchor tweaks and stitch
cons.example: an unchanged A1 losing newness against the rotating A2 accent if never updated

failure_modes: over-elaborating the margin engine with trend features that shorten its sell-window
letting cotton's shrink-and-bag tendency ship A1 off-spec without the post-wash allowance
acceptance_tests: the model states A1's margin/LTV evergreen role, longest sell-window, silhouette/stitch/colour, the ~$70-95 estimate tier and the cotton ~16.5% duty anchor, and the do-not-over-elaborate rule
revisit_triggers: the cotton blend or count is re-specified by yarn
the cotton duty rate changes
A1 sell-through or repeat-rate data lands from selling

base.update_signal: the cotton blend, duty, or A1 repeat-rate data changes

nodes.definition: Model A2, the fine-acrylic 7-12GG value/youth article: the acquisition front door, bought for UGC and reach not contribution, the cheapest legitimate way in and the highest-return SKU. Silhouette is soft-boxy with a slightly-cropped trend-forward option; stitch is rib plus simple abrasion-surviving texture plus plating, strictly no floats; colour carries the rotating trend accent (the youth colour lives here). Price tier ~$45-65 (positioning estimate), feeding off the acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% duty (fact, the outlier). The brand-critical design move is anti-pill-conservative: smooth, tight, no brushed-fuzzy surfaces, because one pilling video is brand-ending and acrylic pills worst.

included: A2's youth acquisition front-door role and high-return profile
the loud trend-accent colour and the slightly-cropped trend-forward fit
the anti-pill-conservative stitch and the ~32% MMF duty anchor
excluded: the acrylic anti-pill finish chemistry (yarn/finishing)
the CAC and channel funnel (brand specialist)

pros.claim: Designing A2 loud and cheap makes it the reach-and-UGC front door without spending contribution margin to acquire
pros.example: an eggplant cropped mock-neck that drives social reach while A1 carries the margin behind it

cons.claim: A loud front-door article risks becoming the house brand and eroding margin if it outshines A1
cons.example: the youth capsule defining the brand so the durable margin engine is forgotten

failure_modes: shipping a brushed or floated acrylic surface that pills and ends the brand
letting A2's loud read drift into the house-brand identity and erode margin and longevity
acceptance_tests: the model states A2's youth acquisition role, the loud trend-accent colour, the smooth-tight no-float anti-pill-conservative stitch, the ~$45-65 estimate tier and the acrylic ~32% duty anchor
revisit_triggers: the acrylic anti-pill spec or duty changes
A2 return-rate or pilling-grade data lands
a trend accent is re-picked for a drop

base.update_signal: the acrylic anti-pill spec, duty, return-rate, or trend accent changes

nodes.definition: Model A3, the thin merino/lambswool Nov-Feb premium capsule: the halo and price-anchor that earns press and makes A1 read as value. It targets the thin true-cold window only (the warm climate's narrow heavy-knit slot). Silhouette is a refined relaxed crew/mock, the cleanest fit; stitch is cable plus fine links-links plus visible fashioning marks as FF-authenticity, with optionally one single intarsia hero; colour is one anchor plus one elevated tonal (eggplant/charcoal). Price tier ~$120-180 (positioning estimate), feeding off the wool 6110.11 ~16% duty (fact). The binding design rule is that cable plus fashioning marks add yarn and linker cost, so A3 must be priced for it; even a few percent nylon or cashmere lifts hand and pill.

included: A3's halo/price-anchor role and the thin Nov-Feb window
cable/links-links/fashioning-marks as priced FF-authenticity
the ~$120-180 tier estimate and the wool ~16% duty anchor
excluded: the merino/lambswool milling and finishing (finishing specialist)
the cable-knittability program (machines specialist)

pros.claim: A premium halo article anchors the price ladder and lets the cotton core read as value
pros.example: a charcoal cable merino crew earning press while making the $70-95 A1 look like a deal

cons.claim: Cable and fashioning marks raise yarn and linker cost, so an under-priced A3 erodes its own margin
cons.example: an A3 priced like A1 that loses money on the extra cable yarn and linker time

failure_modes: under-pricing A3 against the extra cable yarn and linker time it consumes
specifying a cable or fashioning mark that is not stitch-conservative and cannot be knit
acceptance_tests: the model states A3's halo/price-anchor role and Nov-Feb window, cable/links-links/fashioning-marks priced for extra yarn and linker time, the ~$120-180 estimate tier and the wool ~16% duty anchor
revisit_triggers: the merino/lambswool blend or count is re-specified by yarn
the wool duty changes
the cable adds more linker cost than priced

base.update_signal: the merino/lambswool blend, wool duty, or cable cost changes

nodes.definition: Synthesize the three articles as a fibre/role ladder, not a style count: A1 cotton is the margin/LTV engine (longest sell-window, best repeat), A2 acrylic is the cheap front door (bought for reach/UGC, highest return), A3 merino is the halo/price-anchor (press, makes A1 read as value). Each occupies a distinct economic role the others cannot fill, so dropping any one loses a function, not just a SKU. The ladder is also why the design choices differ by article: the fibre carries the role, the role dictates the stitch/colour/price posture, and the three together cross-merchandise on shared anchors and block toward an AOV above the CAC-headroom target.

included: the three distinct economic roles fibre carries
why each role is unfillable by the others
the cross-merchandising toward AOV
excluded: the why-exactly-three SKU-ceiling argument (its own node)
the CAC/AOV model (logistics/brand)

pros.claim: Framing the three as roles not styles explains why each design posture differs and why none can be dropped
pros.example: A2's loudness and A1's evergreen restraint being correct because their roles, not tastes, differ

cons.claim: A clean role ladder can imply the roles are fully separable when they share anchors, block and dye lots
cons.example: treating A3 as wholly independent of A1 when both share the cream anchor and the fit block

failure_modes: designing three styles instead of three roles and losing a function the brand needs
ignoring the cross-merchandising that the shared anchors and block enable
acceptance_tests: the synthesis names the three distinct economic roles fibre carries, why each is unfillable by the others, and the cross-merchandising toward AOV
revisit_triggers: an article's role performance (margin, reach, halo) diverges from plan in selling
a fourth role is proposed
the shared-anchor cross-merchandising economics change

base.update_signal: an article's role performance or a proposed fourth role changes

nodes.definition: State the binding architecture rule carried from the brand: loud youth/hype energy at the front (A2, the acquisition channel) and the durable margin thing (A1) behind it. Design A2 loud and A1 evergreen. The failure this prevents is the loud youth capsule visually becoming the house brand: if it does, margin and longevity erode because the brand is then defined by the highest-return, lowest-contribution article. The rule governs how attention and design emphasis are allocated across the line, keeping the front door loud enough to acquire and the core stable enough to retain.

included: the loud-front/evergreen-behind allocation rule
the house-brand-erosion failure it prevents
the attention-and-emphasis split across the line
excluded: the channel/CAC mechanics of acquisition (brand specialist)
the per-article design detail (article nodes)

pros.claim: Allocating loudness to the front door and restraint to the core protects both acquisition and retention
pros.example: the A2 accent doing the social work while A1 quietly carries the repeat-purchase margin

cons.claim: Holding A1 evergreen while A2 is loud demands discipline the market's attention can undermine
cons.example: the loud A2 capturing all the content and dragging brand identity toward the low-margin article

failure_modes: letting the loud A2 youth capsule become the house brand and erode margin and longevity
making A1 as loud as A2 and losing the evergreen retention anchor
acceptance_tests: the rule states loud A2 at the front and evergreen A1 behind, and the house-brand-erosion failure it prevents
revisit_triggers: the brand identity drifts toward the youth capsule in content/sell-through
the A2-to-A1 conversion path underperforms
a new front-door article is proposed

base.update_signal: the brand identity drift or A2-to-A1 conversion changes

nodes.definition: Argue why exactly three articles: three is simultaneously the role-complete minimum and the MOQ-survivable maximum. Below three forfeits a role (drop A3 and lose the halo/anchor; drop A2 and lose the cheap front door; drop A1 and lose the margin engine). At three, 3 styles x ~3 colours x 6 sizes is already ~54 SKUs, each carrying MOQ plus inventory and working-capital math; a fourth article breaks the dye-lot and working-capital ceiling, while sharing anchors, block and grade keeps the three cross-merchandisable. Three is therefore the smallest set covering all economic roles inside the colour and MOQ ceiling, a derived number, not an aesthetic preference.

included: three as role-complete minimum and MOQ-survivable maximum
the ~54-SKU count and the dye-lot/working-capital ceiling
the shared-anchor cross-merchandising that holds the three together
excluded: the per-SKU inventory and working-capital model (logistics specialist)
the dye-lot economics (yarn specialist)

pros.claim: Deriving three from the role floor and the SKU ceiling makes the line size a defensible computation, not a guess
pros.example: showing a fourth article pushes SKUs past the dye-lot and working-capital ceiling the launch can fund

cons.claim: A fixed three can feel arbitrary if the SKU and dye-lot ceiling assumptions are not re-checked as capital grows
cons.example: holding to three when a larger working-capital base could fund a fourth role-distinct article

failure_modes: adding a fourth article that breaks the dye-lot and working-capital ceiling
cutting to two and forfeiting a distinct economic role
acceptance_tests: the argument shows three is the role-complete minimum and MOQ-survivable maximum, states the ~54-SKU count and the dye-lot/working-capital ceiling, and that a fourth breaks it while a second forfeits a role
revisit_triggers: the SKU count or working-capital base changes materially
the dye-lot ceiling is re-quoted
a genuinely role-distinct fourth article is proposed

base.update_signal: the SKU count, working-capital base, or dye-lot ceiling changes

nodes.definition: Define the sizing math that must be exact: the tech-pack spec is FINISHED-garment (flat/half) measurements, not body, because sweaters carry ~4-6 inch layering ease (our soft-boxy fit at the upper ~5-6 inch end) and confusing the two ships a sweater a full size off. Size set XS-XXL (6), unisex men's-derived block. The four knit measurements at the M base (finished, inches): chest 42 full, body length 28, sleeve length 35.5, bottom hem 20 flat (fact-anchored to public US M charts plus ease). A linear grade applies one increment uniformly: chest +2 in/size (full-chest run 38-48), body +1.5, sleeve +0.75, hem +2, shoulder +0.5; launch linear and let pop-up returns prove whether a non-linear break is needed at XS/XXL.

included: finished-not-body convention and the ~5-6 inch ease
the four knit measurements and the M base
the linear grade increments and the full-chest 38-48 run
excluded: the gauge/shrinkage translation to stitches (its own node)
the pop-up size-curve loop (its own node)

pros.claim: A finished-garment linear grade with a fact-anchored M base gives a defensible spec that does not ship a size off
pros.example: grading the garment chest +2 inches per size on the 42-inch M base rather than confusing it with body chest

cons.claim: A uniform linear grade may not fit the tails if the local body distribution breaks at XS/XXL
cons.example: an XXL that runs short because a non-linear length break the data has not yet justified is missing

failure_modes: specifying body measurements instead of finished and shipping a sweater a full size off
pre-engineering a non-linear grade the pop-up data has not yet justified
acceptance_tests: the math states the finished-not-body convention with ~5-6 inch ease, the four knit measurements and M base, and the linear grade increments with the full-chest 38-48 run
revisit_triggers: pop-up returns argue for a non-linear grade break at XS/XXL
the unisex-block or ease convention is revised
a public US sweater chart the base is cross-checked against updates

base.update_signal: a pop-up grade signal, ease convention, or US sweater chart changes

nodes.definition: Define the knit-unique interaction that turns the inch-grade into a knittable spec: a sweater is knit to a stitch/row count, not cut to a pattern, so each graded dimension must be translated into whole wales/courses at production density before it is programmable (the programmer's job). A 2-inch grade is valid only if it lands on an integer wale count at the production gauge (illustrative estimate: ~9 wales/inch makes +2 inch chest ~+18 wales/side). Spec finished dimensions AFTER relaxation on a washed swatch, build to the post-wash target with <=3-5% residual shrinkage (estimate), with a per-fibre knit-larger allowance (cotton shrinks/bags most, merino mills/relaxes, acrylic is stable but heat-sensitive), balanced ply to kill spirality, and a tolerance on every point or the grade is decorative.

included: the inch-to-whole-wales/courses translation at production density
build-to-post-wash-target on a washed swatch with per-fibre allowance
tolerance-every-point and balanced-ply anti-spirality
excluded: the CAD stitch-count program authoring (machines specialist)
the milling/finishing process (finishing specialist)

pros.claim: Forcing the inch-grade onto integer wales at production density is what makes the spec actually knittable
pros.example: rounding a +2-inch chest to the nearest achievable wale count so the panel programs cleanly

cons.claim: The whole-wales rounding and per-fibre allowance add complexity that is only resolvable once a PPS swatch exists
cons.example: a grade that cannot be finalized until the production stitch density is measured on a physical swatch

failure_modes: specifying an inch grade that does not land on an integer wale count and is unbuildable as drawn
omitting tolerances or the post-wash allowance so the garment ships out of spec after washing
acceptance_tests: the node states the whole-wales/courses translation at production density, the post-wash-target build on a washed swatch with per-fibre allowance, and tolerance-every-point with balanced ply against spirality
revisit_triggers: the production stitch density is measured on a PPS swatch
a per-fibre residual-shrinkage result lands
a spirality or out-of-tolerance defect appears on a sample

base.update_signal: a measured stitch density, shrinkage result, or spirality defect changes

nodes.definition: Define the Turlock pop-ups as the highest-value design input the brand owns: a fitting lab, not just sales. They capture the production size curve (record per fitted customer the size bought and ideally measured chest; the distribution of sizes sold is the XS:S:M:L:XL:XXL ratio to make, and a wrong curve means dead stock in the tails plus stock-outs in the middle). They validate the linear grade and ~5-6 inch ease on the local ~46%-Hispanic Central-Valley body, which may not match the national US chart (estimate). They buy down returns (online ~24% vs ~6% in-store, with size the number-one apparel return reason). And they run as an iteration loop every drop: pop-up curve to adjusted grade/ease and production ratio to next drop, not a one-time calibration.

included: the pop-up size-curve capture as the production ratio
local-body grade/ease validation against the national chart
the return-rate buy-down and the iteration-loop discipline
excluded: the retail/event operations (brand specialist)
the return-cost economics (logistics specialist)

pros.claim: Treating pop-ups as a fitting lab turns the unknown local size curve into measured production quantities
pros.example: recording sizes sold at a pop-up to set the XS:S:M:L:XL:XXL production ratio instead of guessing the curve

cons.claim: A small pop-up sample can mislead the curve if it is read as final before enough fittings accumulate
cons.example: over-fitting the production ratio to one pop-up's attendees rather than a stable distribution

failure_modes: producing on the national chart and missing the local body distribution the pop-ups reveal
treating the size curve as a one-time calibration instead of a per-drop loop
acceptance_tests: the node states the pop-up size-curve capture as the production ratio, local-body grade/ease validation, the ~24%-vs-~6% return buy-down, and the per-drop iteration loop
revisit_triggers: a pop-up runs and produces a size-curve sample
online return-rate-by-size data lands
the local body distribution proves to diverge from the national chart

base.update_signal: a pop-up size-curve, return-rate, or local-body divergence result changes

nodes.definition: Define how trend is ingested and turned into a release clock without chasing the runway. A three-filter funnel: macro (slow, WGSN/Coloro/Pantone plus fashion-week knit, picks the 1-2 accents and confirms the texture-over-colour bet), meso (Everlane/Quince/J.Crew/Massimo Dutti knit plus thrift youth signal, the is-it-shipping check), micro (TikTok FYP/IG Reels/Pinterest, where the brand both reads and publishes). Only signals surviving all three AND the four constraints enter the line; a trend needing 6 colours or a brushed-pill surface is read, noted and declined. The specific Central-Valley-youth hype signals are owned-but-refused as unknown, closed with a listening loop plus pop-up recon. The drop calendar reconciles the warm-CA sell-window, the Ludhiana clock and the trend clock: D1 Fall core (A1, order ~May-Jun), D2 Holiday premium (A3, ~Jul-Aug pre-peak), D3 Youth accent (A2, ~Oct-Nov), D4 Spring transitional (A1-light), all ordered ahead of the Jul-Oct cluster peak.

included: the macro/meso/micro filter funnel and the survives-all-three-plus-constraints rule
the owned-but-refused Central-Valley-youth hype gap
the D1-D4 drop calendar ordered ahead of the Ludhiana peak
excluded: the content-calendar and channel publishing (brand specialist)
the ocean lead-time and order-by economics (logistics specialist)

pros.claim: A three-filter funnel that only admits signals surviving the four constraints stops the brand from chasing un-producible trends
pros.example: noting a 6-colour runway trend and declining it because it cannot pass the colour ceiling

cons.claim: The funnel's reliance on the pop-up and listening loop means the local hype gap stays unknown until instrumented
cons.example: an accent chosen on coastal-national reports that misses the specific Central-Valley youth signal

failure_modes: chasing a runway signal that needs 6 colours or a pill-prone surface the constraints forbid
committing yarn into the Jul-Oct Ludhiana cluster peak instead of ahead of it
acceptance_tests: the node states the macro/meso/micro funnel with the survives-all-three-plus-constraints rule, the refused Central-Valley-youth hype gap, and the D1-D4 calendar ordered ahead of the peak
revisit_triggers: the macro trend palette/silhouette direction updates
the listening loop or pop-up recon yields a local hype signal
the Ludhiana peak window or ocean lead time shifts

base.update_signal: the macro trend, a local hype signal, or the Ludhiana peak window changes

nodes.definition: Frame Flux's place in the pipeline, the framing that prevents the expensive mistake: Flux sits upstream of the programmer, at the idea/look-generation step, not the program. It IS a near-zero-marginal-cost visual-ideation and content engine, and the act of generating is itself the AI-designed-made-by-hands marketing. It IS NOT a CAD/knit programmer, gauge calculator or grading engine, and a Flux image has no stitch count, no GG, no yarn count, no measurement and no shrinkage behaviour, so it will happily render an impossible knit. The brand-specific stake: mistaking a Flux image for a spec ships an un-producible tech pack to Ludhiana and burns a sampling cycle plus dye-lot money. Flux de-risks the idea; it does not de-risk the make. All live parameters are snapshot and re-confirmed on the owner's endpoint, never asserted as fixed fact.

included: Flux as idea/content engine upstream of the programmer
what a render has no information about
the de-risks-the-idea-not-the-make stake and the snapshot parameter discipline
excluded: the specific 8-slot prompt template and live params (operational detail, not a KB node)
the CAD program (machines specialist)

pros.claim: Framing Flux as an idea engine not a compiler prevents shipping an un-producible render as a spec
pros.example: using a render to choose a direction and make content while sending the buildable spec to the programmer separately

cons.claim: The cheap, pretty render is seductive enough that the idea-not-make boundary is easy to forget under deadline
cons.example: treating a gorgeous on-model lookbook image as if it specified the garment

failure_modes: mistaking a Flux image for a spec and shipping an un-producible tech pack to Ludhiana
asserting a live Flux parameter as a fixed fact instead of a snapshot to re-confirm
acceptance_tests: the node states Flux is an idea/content engine upstream of the programmer, that a render carries none of the buildability numbers, the de-risks-idea-not-make stake, and the snapshot parameter discipline
revisit_triggers: the Flux model version or endpoint behaviour changes
image-reference conditioning becomes available on the owner's endpoint
a render is mistaken for a spec in practice

base.update_signal: the Flux model version, endpoint behaviour, or a spec-confusion incident changes

nodes.definition: Define the load-bearing junction where design hands off to yarn and the programmer: a Flux image carries real usable design intent (silhouette/proportion direction, stitch/texture intent, colour story, detailing intent, styling/content direction) but not a single buildability number. The four buildability inputs a pixel cannot give, each filled elsewhere: yarn count plus fibre plus blend ratio (from the yarn spec plus a live quote, T2); true gauge GG plus stitch density (from the stitch vocabulary plus a measured PPS swatch, T2/T3); panel shaping plus stitch-count grade (the inch-grade translated to whole wales/courses by the CAD programmer, T3); finished measurements plus tolerances plus shrinkage allowance (the sizing spec, into the tech pack, T8). Plus three things Flux actively gets wrong, caught in human review before money moves: impossible knits, un-payable colourwork, pill-prone acrylic surfaces.

included: what a render can specify versus the four buildability inputs it cannot
who fills each input (yarn, programmer, swatch, tech pack)
the three things Flux actively gets wrong
excluded: the CAD program authoring (machines specialist)
the yarn count selection (yarn specialist)

pros.claim: Naming the four inputs a pixel cannot give and who fills each closes the gap between a pretty render and a buildable garment
pros.example: routing gauge/density to a PPS swatch and the stitch-count grade to the programmer instead of trusting the image

cons.claim: The bridge depends on disciplines outside design, so a render can stall if the yarn quote or swatch is not yet in hand
cons.example: a chosen look that cannot be specced until the production stitch density is measured

failure_modes: filling a buildability input from the render instead of the yarn spec, swatch, programmer or tech pack
passing an impossible knit, un-payable colourwork or pill-prone surface through to production
acceptance_tests: the bridge lists the four buildability inputs a render cannot give with who fills each, and the three things Flux actively gets wrong caught in human review
revisit_triggers: a buildability input source (yarn quote, swatch, programmer) changes
AI-to-knit-program autonomy is tested on the brand's fabrics
a render-sourced buildability error reaches a sample

base.update_signal: a buildability input source or AI-autonomy test result changes

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: the verdict on whether a designed look may proceed toward a tech pack and PPS swatch. It intersects three lenses: the four upstream constraints (colour budget, warm-CA weight, linker throughput, anti-pill), the buildability bridge (are the four inputs filled from yarn, programmer, swatch and sizing, not the render), and the three traps (kill impossible knits, un-payable colourwork and pill-prone acrylic now). The reconciled rule: choose direction on the on-model render and bank it as content, re-render flat-lay plus tech-flat, run human review against the four constraints and three traps, map intent onto the upstream specs, let the programmer author the stitch-count program, treat the PPS swatch as ground truth, then lock the tech pack; the pop-up sets the size curve. A look that is photogenic but not producible or not profitable is a hold until the gate clears, because photogenic is not producible is not profitable.

included: the three-lens ship/hold intersection
the choose-render to lock-tech-pack workflow
the photogenic-is-not-producible-is-not-profitable rule
excluded: the underlying constraint, bridge and sizing detail (their own nodes)
the AI-to-knit-program-autonomy test result (unknown, refused)

pros.claim: The merged verdict prevents the classic error of shipping a cheap pretty render as a producible spec
pros.example: holding a gorgeous brushed-fuzzy A2 look until the anti-pill trap is cleared on a swatch

cons.claim: A single ship/hold verdict can over-simplify a look whose constraint, buildability and trap reads point different ways
cons.example: a near-buildable A3 cable that passes the colour and pill lenses but fails stitch-conservation review

failure_modes: issuing a ship on a photogenic render before the buildability bridge and three traps are cleared
treating the gate as static when a swatch, programmer read or constraint changes the verdict
acceptance_tests: the verdict intersects the four constraints, the buildability bridge and the three traps into a ship/hold call, states the choose-to-lock workflow, and holds a photogenic-but-not-producible look until the gate clears
revisit_triggers: a PPS swatch or programmer read changes a buildability verdict
an upstream constraint (colour, weight, linker, pill) changes
AI-to-knit-program autonomy on the brand's fabrics is proven or disproven

base.update_signal: a swatch, programmer read, constraint, or AI-autonomy result changes a verdict

cable and intarsia are priced or reserved in the palette because they consume scarce linker time
the 2-anchor-plus-1-2-accent system is engineered to live inside the colour-budget ceiling
the texture-over-colour rule sets colour as evergreen anchors plus restrained rotating accents

A1 carries the two evergreen anchors set by the colour architecture

edges.resolution_rule: design A2 loud at the acquisition front and A1 evergreen behind it; if the youth capsule starts to define the house brand, pull emphasis back to A1 because margin and longevity ride on the core

edges.why_related: the prettiest fuzzy A2 render Flux produces is exactly the pill-prone surface the gate forbids
edges.resolution_rule: let the anti-pill gate overrule the render: reject a fuzzy/brushed A2 look no matter how good it photographs, because the anti-pill grade and tight gauge are the real defence, not the image

edges.why_related: the urge to add an on-trend accent colour pulls against the texture-over-colour, single-colour-body rule
edges.resolution_rule: keep the body single-colour and carry interest with stitch; admit at most one to two rotating accents and prove a hero on sell-through before funding a second dye lot

edges.why_related: A3's cable and fashioning marks deliver the premium look but consume the scarce linker capacity the constraint protects
edges.resolution_rule: permit cable and fashioning marks on A3 as the priced FF-authenticity cue, but price the extra yarn and linker time into the A3 tier and keep them off the higher-volume A1/A2

edges.why_related: the cheap pretty render tempts treating the image as the spec, which the bridge exists to refuse
edges.resolution_rule: treat the render as approved look plus content only; fill the four buildability inputs from the yarn spec, the programmer, the PPS swatch and the sizing math, never from the pixels

edges.why_related: the warm climate caps heavy wool to the thin Nov-Feb window, constraining A3 to a thin premium piece

conflict_axes.name: texture_interest_vs_colour_interest
conflict_axes.description: Interest can be carried by stitch architecture or by colour-count, but the 2-4-colour dye-lot ceiling cannot fund colour, so the two pull against each other.
poles: carry interest with colour and pattern
carry interest with stitch and silhouette
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to texture-over-colour with a single-colour body and at most a contrast tip; admit a colour accent only after sell-through proves it

conflict_axes.name: loud_front_door_vs_evergreen_core
conflict_axes.description: The loud youth A2 drives acquisition while the evergreen A1 drives retention and margin; emphasis can over-tilt to either.
poles: let the loud youth capsule lead the brand
keep the evergreen core as the house identity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: design A2 loud at the front and A1 evergreen behind; never let the youth capsule become the house brand

conflict_axes.name: photogenic_render_vs_producible_spec
conflict_axes.description: A cheap, beautiful Flux render is seductive while a producible spec needs four buildability numbers a pixel lacks; the image can be mistaken for the spec.
poles: ship the photogenic render as the design
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the render as approved look plus content only and fill the four buildability inputs from yarn, programmer, swatch and sizing

conflict_axes.name: anti_pill_safety_vs_acrylic_aesthetics
conflict_axes.description: A softer, fuzzier acrylic surface looks and feels better but pills worst, and one pilling video is brand-ending; safety conflicts with the prettiest render.
poles: chase the soft fuzzy acrylic look
hold the smooth tight anti-pill surface
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the anti-pill gate overrules the look: keep A2 smooth and tight and back it with a contractual anti-pill grade

conflict_axes.name: premium_cable_look_vs_linker_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Cable and fashioning marks deliver A3's premium FF-authenticity but consume scarce linker minutes that are a capacity cost.
poles: add cable and fashioning everywhere for richness
minimize seams and shaping to protect throughput
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reserve cable and fashioning marks for a priced A3 and keep them off the higher-volume A1/A2

conflict_axes.name: linear_grade_simplicity_vs_local_body_fit
conflict_axes.description: A uniform linear grade is simple and launch-ready while the local Central-Valley body may need a non-linear break the data has not yet justified.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: launch linear and let pop-up returns prove whether a non-linear break is needed at XS/XXL

conflict_axes.name: trend_responsiveness_vs_constraint_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Chasing a live runway or micro-trend can demand colours or surfaces the four constraints forbid, so responsiveness conflicts with producibility.
poles: admit only signals that survive the four constraints
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: filter every signal through the macro/meso/micro funnel and decline anything needing 6 colours or a pill-prone surface

conflict_axes.name: three_article_discipline_vs_fourth_role_temptation
conflict_axes.description: A fourth article promises more coverage but breaks the dye-lot and working-capital ceiling that the three-article line is sized to survive.
poles: add a fourth article for more coverage
hold the line at three role-distinct articles
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold at three unless a genuinely role-distinct article and a larger working-capital base can clear the dye-lot ceiling

conflict_axes.name: warm_climate_lightness_vs_premium_wool_window
conflict_axes.description: The warm-California climate wants light fine-gauge knits while the A3 premium halo needs a heavier wool that sells only Nov-Feb.
poles: keep the whole line light fine-gauge
carry a heavier premium wool capsule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the core fine-gauge and confine the heavier merino A3 to the thin Nov-Feb true-cold window

edge_cases.description: A 6-colour jacquard or Fair-Isle look is designed before the dye-lot budget is checked
edge_cases.trigger: a trend or render proposes multi-colour pattern beyond the 2-4-colour ceiling
edge_cases.mitigation: decline colourwork that needs more than the launch dye lots and carry the interest in stitch instead

edge_cases.description: A prettier brushed-fuzzy A2 acrylic render is approved over the smooth tight one
edge_cases.trigger: the soft fuzzy surface photographs best and is chosen for the youth drop
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the fuzzy A2 look no matter how good it looks and hold the smooth tight anti-pill surface with a contractual grade

edge_cases.description: A Flux render is handed to Ludhiana as a tech pack
edge_cases.trigger: a cheap pretty image is mistaken for a buildable spec
edge_cases.mitigation: fill the four buildability inputs from yarn, programmer, swatch and sizing before any tech pack ships, never from the pixels

edge_cases.description: An A3 cable or fashioning mark is rendered that does not conserve stitches and cannot be knit
edge_cases.trigger: Flux produces an impossible cable or shaping that looks plausible
edge_cases.mitigation: catch the impossible knit in human spec review and have the programmer verify the cable is stitch-conserving before sampling

edge_cases.description: Body measurements are specced instead of finished-garment measurements
edge_cases.trigger: a tech pack confuses body chest with garment chest
edge_cases.mitigation: spec finished flat/half measurements with the layering ease built in and sanity-check against body charts

edge_cases.description: The inch-grade is not translated to integer wales and is unbuildable as drawn
edge_cases.trigger: a graded dimension lands between achievable wale counts at production density
edge_cases.mitigation: round each graded dimension to the nearest achievable wale/course count on a measured PPS swatch

edge_cases.description: A cotton A1 ships off-spec after the customer washes it
edge_cases.trigger: the post-wash shrinkage allowance is omitted from the cotton build
edge_cases.mitigation: build to the post-wash target with the per-fibre knit-larger allowance and a residual-shrinkage tolerance in the PO

edge_cases.description: The production size curve is set from the national chart instead of the local pop-up data
edge_cases.trigger: production quantities are committed before a pop-up size curve exists
edge_cases.mitigation: set the XS:S:M:L:XL:XXL production ratio from pop-up fittings and treat the national chart as a launch hypothesis only

edge_cases.description: A live Flux parameter is asserted as a fixed fact in a spec
edge_cases.trigger: a guidance or step value is treated as permanent across model versions
edge_cases.mitigation: tag every Flux parameter snapshot and re-confirm on the owner's live endpoint before it drives spend

edge_cases.description: The loud A2 youth capsule starts to define the house brand
edge_cases.trigger: the youth drop captures all content and brand identity drifts toward it
edge_cases.mitigation: pull design emphasis back to the evergreen A1 core whose margin and longevity the brand rests on

edge_cases.description: A trend accent colour fails a Spanish reading in the ~46%-Hispanic market
edge_cases.trigger: a colour name or slogan-knit ships without a Spanish-language clearance
edge_cases.mitigation: clear every colour name and slogan-knit against a Spanish reading before it ships

edge_cases.description: Yarn is committed into the Jul-Oct Ludhiana cluster peak
edge_cases.trigger: a drop's order-by date falls inside the production cluster peak
edge_cases.mitigation: order each drop's yarn ahead of the Jul-Oct peak per the drop calendar's order-by dates

workflow.action: Fix the four upstream constraints before any aesthetics
workflow.description: State the colour-budget ceiling, warm-CA weight, linker throughput and anti-pill gate and what each forbids/forces
workflow.gate: all four constraints are stated with the design consequence each pre-decides

workflow.description: Convert the colour ceiling into the texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print, single-colour-body rule
workflow.gate: the rule is stated and tied to the colour ceiling as its source

workflow.action: Set the shared block and stitch/colour spine
workflow.description: Define the soft-boxy unisex block with two variants, the tiered stitch palette and the anchor-plus-accent colour system
workflow.gate: the block, stitch tiers and colour architecture are stated inside the constraints

workflow.action: Design A1 the evergreen cotton margin engine
workflow.description: Specify A1's silhouette/stitch/colour, ~$70-95 tier and the do-not-over-elaborate rule with the cotton ~16.5% duty
workflow.gate: A1's role, posture, tier estimate and cotton duty anchor are stated

workflow.action: Design A2 the loud anti-pill-conservative front door
workflow.description: Specify A2's loud trend accent, smooth-tight no-float stitch, ~$45-65 tier and the acrylic ~32% duty
workflow.gate: A2's acquisition role, anti-pill stitch, tier estimate and acrylic duty anchor are stated

workflow.action: Design A3 the priced merino halo
workflow.description: Specify A3's cable/links-links/fashioning marks priced for linker time, ~$120-180 tier and the wool ~16% duty
workflow.gate: A3's halo role, priced cable, tier estimate and wool duty anchor are stated

workflow.action: Compose the fibre-role ladder and architecture
workflow.description: Frame the three as distinct economic roles, apply the loud-front rule and derive why exactly three
workflow.gate: the three roles, the loud-front rule and the three-as-derived-number are stated

workflow.action: Build the finished-garment grade and knit translation
workflow.description: Specify the finished-not-body four measurements, the linear grade and the gauge/shrinkage whole-wales translation
workflow.gate: the M base, linear grade, whole-wales translation and per-fibre shrinkage allowance are stated

workflow.action: Wire the pop-up fitting lab and trend-to-drop clock
workflow.description: Set the pop-up size-curve loop and the three-filter trend funnel feeding the D1-D4 drop calendar
workflow.gate: the pop-up loop and the constraint-filtered drop calendar are stated

workflow.action: Frame Flux and the buildability bridge
workflow.description: State Flux as idea/content engine upstream of the programmer and the four buildability inputs a render cannot give
workflow.gate: the idea-not-compiler framing and the four buildability inputs with their owners are stated

workflow.description: Intersect the four constraints, the buildability bridge and the three traps into a ship/hold verdict ending at a locked tech pack
workflow.gate: the verdict states the constraint, buildability and trap reads and holds a photogenic-but-not-producible look until the gate clears

dominance_rules.rule: The upstream constraints dominate any aesthetic choice
dominance_rules.rationale: the design space is generated from the colour budget, warm-CA weight, linker throughput and anti-pill gate before a moodboard is opened
dominance_rules.trigger: an aesthetic preference conflicts with a constraint
dominance_rules.action: let the constraint pre-decide and design inside it, banking the trend alignment as coincidence

dominance_rules.rule: The anti-pill gate dominates the prettier acrylic render
dominance_rules.rationale: one pilling video is brand-ending and acrylic pills worst, so the gate is brand-ending not a preference
dominance_rules.trigger: a fuzzy/brushed A2 look is chosen for being photogenic
dominance_rules.action: reject it and hold the smooth tight surface with a contractual anti-pill grade

dominance_rules.rule: The buildability bridge dominates the cheap pretty render
dominance_rules.rationale: a Flux pixel cannot specify the four buildability inputs and actively renders impossible knits
dominance_rules.trigger: an image is treated as a producible spec
dominance_rules.action: fill the four inputs from yarn, programmer, swatch and sizing before a tech pack ships

dominance_rules.rule: The evergreen core dominates the loud front door for brand identity
dominance_rules.rationale: margin and longevity ride on A1, so the youth capsule must not become the house brand
dominance_rules.trigger: brand identity drifts toward the loud A2 capsule
dominance_rules.action: pull design emphasis back to the evergreen A1 core

dominance_rules.rule: Finished-garment measurements dominate body measurements in the tech pack
dominance_rules.rationale: confusing the two ships a sweater a full size off
dominance_rules.trigger: a spec uses body chest where garment chest is required
dominance_rules.action: spec finished flat/half measurements with layering ease and sanity-check against body charts

dominance_rules.rule: The PPS swatch dominates the render and the screen colour as ground truth
dominance_rules.rationale: a physical swatch measures real gauge, density, shrinkage and pilling that pixels and monitors cannot
dominance_rules.trigger: a buildability or colour decision rests on an image
dominance_rules.action: defer to the measured PPS swatch and a lab-dip dye shade, not the render

dominance_rules.rule: Saturation at three dominates the temptation of a fourth article
dominance_rules.rationale: a fourth article breaks the dye-lot and working-capital ceiling the line is sized to survive
dominance_rules.action: default to holding at three role-distinct articles unless a larger capital base clears the ceiling

dominance_rules.rationale: without a tolerance on every measurement point the grade rule is decorative
dominance_rules.trigger: a graded spec omits per-point tolerances
dominance_rules.action: attach a tolerance to every measurement and reject out-of-tolerance samples

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the colour-budget ceiling before designing any colourwork
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a multi-colour pattern being designed and then cut when the dye-lot budget cannot fund it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fill the four buildability inputs from their owners before any tech pack ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an un-producible render reaching Ludhiana and burning a sampling cycle plus dye-lot money

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the anti-pill gate to A2 at the render-selection step, not after sampling
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a pill-prone acrylic surface being approved and triggering a brand-ending return wave

anti_rework_rules.rule: Spec finished-garment measurements with ease from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a body-measurement tech pack shipping a sweater a full size off and being remade

anti_rework_rules.rule: Translate the inch-grade to integer wales on a measured swatch before programming
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unbuildable grade that the programmer cannot run and must send back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Price cable and fashioning marks into the A3 tier when the stitch is chosen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an under-priced A3 losing margin on extra cable yarn and linker time

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the production size curve from pop-up data, not the national chart
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dead stock in the size tails and stock-outs in the middle from a wrong curve

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every Flux parameter snapshot and re-confirm on the live endpoint
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stale guidance/step value driving spend after a model version changes its behaviour

iteration_protocol.trigger: a PPS swatch measures the production stitch density, shrinkage and pilling grade
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimated gauge/density and shrinkage allowance with measured values and re-confirm the anti-pill grade and the whole-wales grade translation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Turlock pop-up produces a local size curve and fit-return data
iteration_protocol.action: revise the linear grade and ease, set the production size ratio and decide whether a non-linear break is needed at XS/XXL

iteration_protocol.trigger: the dye-lot MOQ, per-colour cost or working-capital base changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the colour ceiling, the colour architecture and the why-exactly-three SKU math

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Flux model version or endpoint behaviour changes, or image-reference conditioning becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm the snapshot parameters and the idea-not-compiler framing and re-test capsule-consistency

iteration_protocol.trigger: a US sweater duty rate or the fibre blend for an article changes
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected article's duty anchor and price tier

iteration_protocol.trigger: the macro trend palette/silhouette updates or the listening loop yields a Central-Valley-youth hype signal
iteration_protocol.action: re-pick the rotating accent and re-time the drop calendar against the Ludhiana peak

iteration_protocol.trigger: AI-to-knit-program autonomy on the brand's fabrics is tested and proven or disproven
iteration_protocol.action: update whether Flux stays strictly upstream of the programmer or can author a runnable graded program

priority_rationale: The four upstream constraints come first because they generate the entire design space before any aesthetic choice; the texture-over-colour spine and the shared block/stitch/colour system next, because they convert the constraints into a coherent design grammar; the three articles and the fibre-role ladder then apply that grammar to concrete A1/A2/A3 postures with the loud-front rule and the why-exactly-three derivation; the finished-garment grade, gauge/shrinkage translation, pop-up loop and trend/drop calendar make the design buildable and sellable on the right clock; and the Flux ideation role, buildability bridge and merged producibility gate come last because they compose every upstream output into the ship/hold verdict that protects against confusing a cheap pretty render with a knittable garment.
